previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of pseudotumor cerebri s/p VP shunt placement presented with persistent right lower quadrant abdominal pain, raising concern for shunt-related complications. Imaging including CT abdomen/pelvis, shunt series, and pelvic ultrasound showed no acute surgical or shunt-related cause, with findings stable compared to prior studies. The pain was determined to be chronic and not related to the shunt, with no evidence of infection, obstruction, or inflammation. She was managed with pain control using gabapentin and oxycodone, a bowel regimen for stool burden, and resolution of mild acute kidney injury secondary to reduced oral intake. Her condition improved, and she was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up in pain psychology and with her primary care physician for ongoing management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ female with pmhx of pseudotumor cerebri with VP shunt 
placed ___ and recent admission for RLQ pain, presenting with 
RLQ pain.

# RLQ pain.  Persistent since the placement of the shunt.  
During recent admission, patient had thorough work up, including 
VP shunt series, CT abd/pelvis, and pelvis ultrasound, which 
showed appropriate location and function of the VP shunt without 
lesions that would explain her pain.  She was evaluated by 
neurosurgery who thought that given the recent placement of her 
shunt, it is not unusual to see some residual discomfort, which 
is expected to improve with time.  Patient does not think 
oxycodone helps with her pain.  Therefore, the pain service also 
evaluated patient for non-opioid options.  Gabapentin dose was 
increased to 400 mg TID from 300 mg TID.  Lidocaine patch was 
provided.  She thought these helped to relief some pain.  
Gabapentin may be titrated to 600 mg TID as needed in the 
future.  This dose was based on her renal function.  Slow 
titration was chosen as patient is already on multiple sedating 
medications.  It was recommended to her that management of her 
RLQ pain will require time and multiple disciplines; therefore, 
it would be important for her to follow up with the physicians 
as scheduled, so that she would get the appropriate care.  

# Pseudotumor cerebri & Migraine.  Similar to her previous 
headaches; although overall frequency and intensity of headache 
improved since VP shunt placement.  VP shunt was confirmed to be 
in the right location both at the last admission and this 
admission.  She was given her home medications.

# Visual disturbance.  She complained of some vision blurriness 
and diplopia while in house; however, neurological exam revealed 
normal EOM, diplopia with distance only, and diplopia with left 
eye only.  The double appears on the right of the object with 
distance and the double appears on the left of the object with 
her left eye only.  Her neurological exam was otherwise 
non-focal.  She was also able to read the paper and menu without 
difficulty despite having blurry vision.  Based on the exam and 
her description, patient was reassured.  She was recommended to 
obtain a formal ophthalmology evaluation.

Chronic Issues:
# Hypertension.  Patient was continued on home amlodipine and 
enalapri.
# Hyperelipidemia.  She was continued on simvastatin.  
# T2DM.  Her home glyburide was held while in house and she 
received insulin sliding scale.  She was discharged on 
glyburide.
# GERD.  She was continued on omeprazole
# Depression & Anxiety.  She was continued on amitryptiline, 
citalopram, and lorazepam.

# Pending: none
# Issues to address:
- consider narcotics contract if she is going to be on pain 
medications indefinitely
- monitor chronic anemia
